summary: This document defines common types and groupings in YANG for modules that model Layer 0 optical Traffic Engineering configuration and state, such as Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs) and flexi-grid DWDM networks. Other modules import them.

plainLanguage.summary: Optical networks send data as colors of light in a fiber. This document collects shared building blocks that other descriptions of those light networks can reuse.

subtitle: Shared YANG building blocks for describing optical networks that use fixed and flexible wavelength grids.

tldr.problem: Each YANG model of a Layer 0 optical network would need the same definitions of grids, channel spacings and label ranges.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the module ietf-layer0-types, a set of derived types, identities and groupings for WSON and flexi-grid DWDM networks, meant to be imported by other modules.
tldr.outcome: Layer 0 models can reuse one agreed vocabulary. The module defines no readable or writable data nodes of its own.

today: RFC 9093 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It is the definition of the ietf-layer0-types module.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
YANG (RFC 7950) is a data modeling language for configuration data, state data, remote procedure calls and notifications, used with protocols such as NETCONF (RFC 6241). It has a small set of built-in types and lets authors derive more.

This RFC introduces common types and groupings derived from the built-in ones. They are meant for modeling Traffic Engineering (TE) and non-TE features of Layer 0 optical networks, in models defined outside this document. They apply to Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs) and flexi-grid Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) networks. The module conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342).
sections.plainLanguage: Many people need to describe the same kind of light-based network. This document writes down the common words once, so everyone can use them.

sections.title: Module Contents
sections.content:
The module is named ietf-layer0-types and uses the prefix l0-types. The RFC lists these reusable pieces:

  • l0-grid-type: a base identity for the grid type.
  • dwdm-ch-spc-type and cwdm-ch-spc-type: base identities for DWDM and Coarse Wavelength Division Multiplexing (CWDM) channel spacing.
  • Groupings for WSON: wson-label-start-end, wson-label-hop and wson-label-step, plus l0-label-range-info for the label range.
  • Groupings for flexi-grid: flexi-grid-label-start-end, flexi-grid-label-hop, flexi-grid-label-range-info and flexi-grid-label-step.

The label groupings supply the WSON-specific or flexi-grid-specific parts of the label-start, label-end and label-hop information that the generic topology model (RFC 8795) defines.
sections.plainLanguage: The module is a parts shelf. Some parts say which kind of grid you have, some say how far apart the colors are, and some describe a range of colors.

sections.title: Grids, Channel Spacing and Slot Widths
sections.content:
A grid is the set of allowed positions for optical channels. The module defines three grid identities derived from l0-grid-type: wson-grid-dwdm, wson-grid-cwdm and flexi-grid-dwdm.

Channels are located by an integer. For DWDM, the nominal central frequency is f = 193100.000 GHz + N x channel spacing, where 193100.000 GHz is the ITU-T anchor frequency. For CWDM, the wavelength is 1471 nm + N x channel spacing. Flexi-grid uses the same frequency anchor with a value flexi-n, and a second integer flexi-m sets the slot width as M x SWG in GHz, where SWG is the slot width granularity.

Channel spacings are identities. DWDM has dwdm-100ghz, dwdm-50ghz, dwdm-25ghz and dwdm-12p5ghz. CWDM has cwdm-20nm, the only CWDM value defined. Flexi-grid has flexi-ch-spc-6p25ghz, and its slot width granularity is flexi-swg-12p5ghz.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of a piano. The grid says which keys exist, the spacing says how far apart they are, and a number says which key you mean. Flexi-grid lets you press several neighboring keys together as one wide note.

sections.title: Label Ranges, Hops and Steps
sections.content:
The groupings use YANG choice statements so a model can describe a DWDM or CWDM label for WSON. In a label hop, a DWDM channel is either a single channel with one dwdm-n or a super channel with a list of subcarrier values. A when condition makes a DWDM or CWDM leaf valid only when the grid type matches.

For flexi-grid, flexi-grid-frequency-slot combines flexi-n and flexi-m. A flexi-grid label range adds a container with slot-width-granularity (default 12.500 GHz), min-slot-width-factor (default 1) and max-slot-width-factor. The maximum must be greater than or equal to the minimum, and if it is not given it equals the minimum. Slot widths are the factor times the granularity.
sections.plainLanguage: These pieces let you say 'a stretch of colors from here to there', 'the exact colors used on one hop', and 'how big each step is'. A wide flexi-grid slot is just a minimum and maximum number of small steps.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has registered the XML namespace URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-layer0-types in the IETF XML Registry, with the IESG as registrant contact. It also registered the YANG module ietf-layer0-types in the YANG Module Names registry, with prefix l0-types and this document as the reference. The module's revision is dated 2021-08-13 and is described as the initial version.
sections.plainLanguage: The module was added to the official lists under its own name so nobody else uses it by mistake.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
YANG data is accessed through protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF. NETCONF's mandatory-to-implement secure transport is Secure Shell (SSH), and RESTCONF's is TLS. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) can restrict which users may use which operations and content.

This module defines only common types and groupings, so no object in it can be read or written. The risk comes from modules that import it: the resulting schema may have writable or readable data nodes that matter to network operations if misused. The RFC says those considerations belong in the importing documents, and that access to sensitive nodes should be managed. The security considerations of YANG 1.1 also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: This box of parts is harmless by itself. Whoever builds something with the parts has to think about who may touch the finished thing.
